summary: Municipal Infrastructure Maintenance (110-4013) counted as a tax in Other taxes
detail: The budget documents label it Municipal Infrastructure Maintenance (about $62-197K a year); the city's audits report it as Telecommunications tax, and as a tax. Before 2026-10-22 it was treated as an excluded fee.

summary: budget documents call this Municipal Infrastructure Maintenance; counted as a tax (decided 2026-10-22), as the audit presents it
detail: Shown as its own group in the audit-basis tables and counted in totals.

summary: Telecom Tax Rebate (01-5-110-4013) sits in the expense block, is not in the printed revenue total, and is left out of the series
detail: At most $10,783 a year. It is the rebate of the 110-4013 tax; open item whether to treat it as an offset. Shares an object code with the revenue line, hence flow contra_expense.

summary: Health Insurance Reimbursement is in the expense block and not in the printed revenue total
detail: Kept as a contra_expense account so it cannot be confused with revenue. The city counts it as a negative expense: it reduces the printed Gen Admin Personnel & Benefit subtotal and the department and fund expense totals (e.g. FY2027 -$950,000), so sums of expense lines must include contra_expense facts to tie to the printed totals.

summary: Printed 01-5-330-4940 through FY2019, 01-4- in FY2020-23, 01-5- again in FY2024
detail: Same line, second account segment flips between 4 and 5; account keys therefore ignore it (entity.json key_segments). Also affects 310-4940 and 310-4950.

summary: City prints 01-4-1104114 (missing hyphen) for Real Estate Tax to Developer
detail: Printed in the FY2026 budget and mirrored in the FY2027 file; normalised by entity.json typo_fixes.

summary: $26,000 Forestry revenue line printed with no label or account number
detail: Inserted by an add_row override (01-4-340-UNLABELED). The FY2026 audit's Grants = documents' 436,000 + 26,000, so it is a grant, not a tax.
evidence: budget FY2026 page image; audit FY2026

summary: Local motor fuel tax is inside the audit's Grants line FY2020-FY2025, its own line only in FY2026
detail: Audit Grants budget equals the documents' grants + motor fuel to the dollar, so motor fuel is left out of every audit-basis year to keep the series continuous.

summary: hotel/motel + auto rental + cannabis; local motor fuel tax excluded in every year (audit reports it inside Grants FY2020-25)
detail: See EX-motor-fuel-grants.

summary: audit reports sales and use combined; later audits report them separately (summed here)
detail: Sales and use are summed in every year so the series is continuous.

summary: Audit replacement tax is net of the distribution to pensions
detail: Budget side: 110-4120 + 140-4120 minus the pension distribution 110-4121. Budget-document actuals for the pension distribution look like budget copies in FY2019-20 and FY2022-25, so audited actuals are the better series.

summary: FY2014 audit sales tax is net of a $35,000 developer rebate
detail: The only comparable group-year where audit original budget differs from the budget documents' adopted budget (134 of 135 match). Later audits do not net developer rebates.

summary: FY2025 document's FY2024 utility tax column holds the FY2023 values, not the adopted budget
detail: FY2024 utility $2,160,000 per the audits (original and final). FY2025 document restates 1,092,591 / 846,396 / 148,176 (the FY23 values) vs the adopted 1,100,000 / 925,000 / 135,000. Also 150-4940: 158,478 vs 158,480. budget_prior_doc differs from adopted; adopted (own-document) is used.
evidence: audit FY2024 original and final budgets

summary: FY2026 document's FY2025 Audit and IMRF levy columns differ from the adopted budget
detail: Audit 20,039 vs 20,000 and IMRF 65,088 vs 65,000 in the FY2026 document; the audits show the own-document (earlier) figures were adopted. The same column also shows Heritage Days (110-4901) 31,781 vs 0, not a tax.

summary: Buchanan Street Strolls (01-4-615-*) is omitted from the city's printed fund total in some columns
detail: FY2021, FY2022's FY21 columns, and the actual column of FY2023 and FY2024. Flagged not_in_printed_total; not a tax.

summary: City's printed FY2016 fund total is $1 off its own rows
detail: allow_diff override. Cent-rounding differences of $1-3 also occur in printed Actual totals.

summary: No FY2014 budget document extracted; FY2014 adopted figures come from document FY2015's prior-year column
detail: The FY2014 audit original budget agrees.

summary: Values corrected by eye against page images are recorded in data/belvidere_il/overrides/
detail: Each override row carries its reason. FY2021 needed 8; recurring OCR errors are a leading 1 read as 4 and 6 read as 8.

summary: Health Insurance Reimbursement (110-4540) is revenue-coded but counted as negative expense in the city's printed expense subtotals
detail: Appears in the Gen Admin personnel block between salary and benefit lines. Facts carry it as flow contra_expense; reconciliation (govbudget.reconcile) adds it to expenses.
evidence: budget page images; FY2027 Gen Admin personnel subtotal ties only with it

summary: Reimb of Seized Vehicle Fee, Heritage Days and the ARPA transfer out are printed but left out of the city's Gen Admin expense total
detail: FY2021 actual: 7901 (300) and 7902 (4,225) omitted; FY2022 actual: 7902 (100,117) omitted; FY2023 actual: 7902 (96,131) and 9990 ARPA transfer (929,431) omitted from the printed Total General Administration Expenses and NET lines. The lines are real expenses and are kept in the facts; the printed totals understate them.
evidence: budget FY2023-25 page images; amounts equal the gaps exactly

summary: Buchanan Street Strolls expense lines are left out of the printed fund expense total (the STROLLS NET line includes them)
detail: FY2021 budget columns (22,250) and FY2021-FY2022 actual columns (19,706 and 14,399). Same pattern as the Strolls revenue lines (EX-strolls-total).

summary: The printed fund expense total is $5,050 above the sum of its lines in FY2021 budget and FY2021-FY2024 actual columns, after the omitted lines are removed
detail: Every department NET line ties to its rows, so the gap is in the fund total only. In the FY2021 budget column the Strolls NET is also (5,050), which may be related; not located. See data/belvidere_il/reconciliation.csv.

summary: FY2024 ordinance prints a stale Gen Admin Personnel & Benefit subtotal (824,817); its lines sum to 901,587
detail: The FY23 column prints 824,816 for the same subtotal, so the FY24 figure was carried over. The department total, NET line and fund total inherit the 76,770 gap. Lines are used as printed; control totals keep the printed figure.

detail: Both documents' printed totals tie to their own lines, so this is an amended or restated budget in the later document, not an OCR error. Use basis adopted for the budget as passed; prior_doc_budget shows the later restatement.
evidence: extract comparison FY2016-FY2027: all other prior-year expense columns (about 125-135 cells a year) match exactly

summary: FY2025 document's prior-year expense column differs from the FY2024 adopted budget for these accounts
detail: Both documents' printed totals tie to their own lines, so this is an amended or restated budget in the later document, not an OCR error. Use basis adopted for the budget as passed; prior_doc_budget shows the later restatement.
evidence: extract comparison FY2016-FY2027: all other prior-year expense columns (about 125-135 cells a year) match exactly

summary: FY2026 document's prior-year expense column differs from the FY2025 adopted budget for these accounts
detail: Both documents' printed totals tie to their own lines, so this is an amended or restated budget in the later document, not an OCR error. Use basis adopted for the budget as passed; prior_doc_budget shows the later restatement.

summary: Expense cells the extractor corrected without a page-image check are flagged auto_resolved / auto_resolved_digit
detail: extract_budget.py adopts another reading of a cell (other OCR prep, or the neighbouring year's document, which prints the same budget figure) only when it makes a failing printed total tie exactly; auto_resolved_digit (a single-digit OCR confusion) is the weaker evidence. Eyeballed corrections are in overrides/.

summary: Expense categories follow object-code ranges (5xxx personnel ... 9xxx transfers); the city's printed Personnel/Contractual/Supplies subtotals are kept as control totals, not reproduced as categories
detail: The city prints some 79xx, 8xxx and 9xxx lines outside its three subtotals, and the subtotals differ by department.

summary: The audit's General Fund expenditures exclude the budget's transfers out (object codes 9xxx, and the 751-8040 transfer to Capital)

evidence: audit_expenses_vs_budget.csv: 179 of 182 department group-years match the budget to the dollar with these rules

detail: Health Insurance in the FY2015 audit is 238,684 vs the budget's gross 356,033 (difference 117,349 = the reimbursement). The budget always prints it in the expense block as negative expense.

summary: Sales Tax to Developer is a revenue offset in the budget but an expenditure ("Sales tax incentive", Economic development) in the audit
detail: The real estate tax rebate to developers (110-4114) stays netted in the audit. The FY2014 audit netted the $35,000 sales tax rebate into sales tax revenue instead (see the revenue notes).
evidence: audit FY2026 expenditure schedule; budget FY2026 revenue lines

summary: The audit books the Utility Tax department's capital projects (Downtown streetscape, Tripp Road, Bellwood detention basin, ...) under Economic development
detail: Budget department 751 (Utility Tax, object codes 805x-806x) is compared together with departments 610 and 615 (audit_expenditure_map.csv).
evidence: audit FY2016-FY2019 expenditure schedules vs budget dept 751

summary: FY2014 audit original budget has a $700 City Engineering vehicle repair line that the FY2015 document's prior-year column prints as 0
detail: Both extractions tie to their printed totals.
evidence: audit FY2014; budget FY2015 prior-year column

summary: FY2017 audit original budget for Street Gas and Oil is 75,000; the FY2017 budget document prints 85,000
detail: The only department-year (besides the $700 and a $1 rounding) where the audit original budget differs from the adopted budget; both extractions tie to their printed totals.
evidence: audit FY2017 p120; budget FY2017 page 6

summary: The governmental funds statements show different fund columns in different years: General and Total governmental funds are always there; Motor Fuel Tax and Capital Projects appear as their own columns only in some years
detail: Use fund General or Total governmental funds for series; nonmajor and other columns are not comparable across years (fund_statements.csv labels each cell with its fund).

summary: FY2016 restates the General Fund beginning balance by a $207,812 prior period adjustment
detail: Beginning balance as printed 11,003,529 equals FY2015 ending; restated beginning 10,795,717. fund_balance_summary.csv uses the restated figure, so its rollforward_diff for FY2016 is -207,812.

summary: The FY2012 audit labels fund balance in its own pre-GASB 54 way ("by tax levy", "Minimum fund balance", ...), so nonspendable/restricted/assigned/unassigned are not comparable for FY2012 (the 3.7M "unassigned" is its General fund line)
detail: Totals (cash, assets, liabilities, total fund balance, net change) are comparable.

summary: FY2012 statement totals are $1 off their fund columns, and General Fund revenues/expenditures differ from the schedules by $1 and $3
detail: Cents rounding in the source (overrides audit_fund_FY2012.csv).

summary: Water / Sewer Fund (61) account keys carry the fund ("61:810-5010") and departments are fund-scoped, because department codes repeat across funds (110 is also Water / Sewer General Administration)
detail: departments.csv has a fund_code column. In FY2015-FY2020 the budget prints the Collection System expense lines (printed 61-5-830 in later years) under the sewer code 820; they are assigned to dept 830 by the "Collection System Expenses" heading (flag dept_from_heading) so each key is unique.

summary: The depreciation and bond payment set-asides are unnumbered expense lines in the budget (they move cash to the depreciation and bond funds); this project gives them pseudo accounts 61:DDD-DEPSA and 61:DDD-BONDSA
detail: They are in the printed Total Department Expenses but are not operating expenses in the audit.

summary: The budget's cash sub-ledgers after the department blocks (bond reserves, connection fees / deposits, depreciation funding, bond payments) are not extracted
detail: Beginning and ending cash of the department blocks are control totals (beginning_cash / ending_cash); the cash roll-forward (beginning + net + change in receivables) differs from ending cash by other fund transactions in several years and is reported as a note, not a failure.

summary: The audit's Water and Sewer operating expenses equal the budget's expense lines without the set-asides, transfers out (9999) and the card processing fee (4595, netted against revenue in the audit)
detail: 31 of 33 department-years FY2016-FY2026 match to the dollar (build_audit_ws_compare.py).

summary: FY2018 Collection System salaries: the audit original budget is 292,295, the budget documents (FY2018 and FY2019) print 287,187
detail: Both extractions tie to their printed totals; a $5,108 difference in the sources.

summary: The FY2020 audit original budget for Sewer includes $5,204,000 of capital outlay (equipment) that the budget carries in its depreciation funding sub-ledger, not in the Sewer expense lines
detail: Excluding it the Sewer budgets agree.
evidence: audit FY2020 schedule of operating expenses

summary: The audit's Water and Sewer summary schedule is on the budgetary basis (actual operating expenses include capital outlay and principal payments) with a reconciliation to the GAAP change in net position; the detail schedule of operating expenses is not reconciled to the summary's actual column
detail: Budget columns of both schedules agree with the budget documents; only the actual columns differ in basis. FY2016-FY2017 print one change in net position (no GAAP adjustments).
